analysis.title: Market volatility reinforces case for portfolio resilience (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: US equities fell again on Thursday. The S&P 500 closed down 2% and the Nasdaq Composite down 2.3%. The sell-off continued in Asia on Friday, with the Nikkei 225 down over 5% and Taiwan's benchmark index down 6.2%.

The decline was broad. All major S&P 500 sectors traded lower, and decliners substantially outnumbered advancers on both the NYSE and Nasdaq. UBS links the selling to persistent pressure on chipmakers and cloud companies as investors question the scale of AI infrastructure investment.

Minutes of the Fed's October meeting indicated nearly all policymakers expected further tightening to be necessary if the economy evolves as anticipated. Markets priced a near certainty of a 25bp hike in December.

Hunterbrook published a short-sell report on AMD (-7.7%) over concerns that its China business may be affected by stricter US chip restrictions. NVIDIA (-3.3%) extended recent losses despite an upbeat revenue forecast earlier in the week.

UBS does not think the economic expansion, the corporate earnings cycle or the structural AI investment story has broken. The 2027 base case is near-trend growth, rising profits, more AI investment and moderating inflation later in the year.

UBS recently downgraded global equities from Attractive to Neutral, citing elevated expectations, high index concentration and a wider range of AI outcomes. The AI debate is shifting from whether investment continues to whether it can generate enough revenue and shareholder returns.

Cumulative US tech AI infrastructure investment could approach USD 5tr by the end of 2028. UBS estimates AI model and application revenues must reach at least USD 1.5tr by 2030 for an adequate return. Competition, price cuts, costly monetization and open-weight models may threaten returns.
UBS expects 25bp US hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 but no prolonged tightening cycle. Higher rates should weigh on consumer demand, and base effects should moderate underlying inflation.

Equities: UBS expects about 15% S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027. The top 10 companies are 39% of the index. The Eurozone is the preferred region (15% 2027 earnings growth forecast, lower valuation than the US). UBS favors industrials and health care, and says US equal-weight strategies can reduce tech concentration.

Within US tech, UBS favors financially strong hyperscalers with visible AI monetization and select leaders in compute, foundry, semiconductor equipment and infrastructure software. It is cautious on leveraged capacity providers, lower-quality suppliers and companies whose valuations depend on persistent bottlenecks or distant cash flows.

Fixed income: UBS favors intermediate duration (two to 10 years) and sees the best return opportunity in EM and high yield bonds. EM sovereign yields about 7.1%, EM corporate about 7.0% and US high yield about 8.3%.

Volatility: UBS advises using volatility rather than fearing it. Structured strategies can limit losses, generate income or allow measured participation, and higher implied volatility may raise their appeal. UBS cautions about capital loss, issuer, liquidity and opportunity-cost risks.

Gold fell 1.3% on Friday to about USD 3,575/oz, the lowest since September 2025. It is down nearly 8% week to date, on track for its biggest weekly decline since March. UBS attributes this to stronger US labor data, above-consensus inflation and hawkish Fed comments about outsized rate increases.

UBS sees an attractive risk-reward for a long gold position, or selling volatility, and expects gold to gravitate back toward USD 5,000/oz in late 2027. It says the market may be overestimating the level and duration of higher rates, and that gold is technically oversold.

Alibaba reported Q3 cloud revenue growth of 53% y/y, with external cloud revenue up more than 60% y/y and a margin of roughly 14.5%, up from below 10% two quarters earlier. Management kept its USD 100bn cloud revenue ambition for 2030.

Tencent said cloud growth accelerated to around 35% y/y, but higher capex led to a second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow. Spending is near a quarterly peak but could stay elevated for several quarters.

UBS favors China tech areas where earnings visibility, policy support and demand align: onshore semiconductor equipment vendors, foundries and other hardware companies benefiting from AI chip localization.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS says the AI investment story has not broken. It expects further AI investment growth and about 15% S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027. Alibaba's cloud revenue grew 53% y/y with margin up to about 14.5%.
tension_points.bear_case: Cumulative AI infrastructure investment could approach USD 5tr by 2028, and AI revenues must reach at least USD 1.5tr by 2030 for an adequate return. Competition, price cuts, costly monetization and open-weight models may threaten returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI model and application revenues falling short of the USD 1.5tr by 2030 needed for an adequate industry return.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects inflation to level off and activity to moderate in 2027, shifting rate expectations from hikes to a pause and then cuts later in the year. Central bank demand and recovering jewelry demand should stabilize gold.
tension_points.bear_case: Stronger labor data, above-consensus inflation and hawkish Fed comments reinforced expectations of further hikes, pressuring gold to its lowest since September 2025.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rate expectations continuing to rise toward larger or prolonged hikes rather than shifting to a pause in 2027.
